other.summary: Directory index lookup now goes through _lookup_path, so PermissionError->401 and ENAMETOOLONG->404; small behavior change the PR description doesn't mention
other.reason: True (old code called self.lookup_path(index_path) with no error mapping), but this is a consistency improvement, not a defect.

other.summary: Suggests adding a test for POST to a directory without a trailing slash (returns 405, no redirect)
other.reason: Behavior is as described and no such test exists in the PR, but this is a test-coverage suggestion only.

other.summary: Docs claim that path operations have higher priority may hold only if the frontend is mounted after the routes
other.reason: APIRouter.frontend appends the _FrontendRouteGroup to self._low_priority_routes (routing.py:2519), so frontend routes always come after regular routes regardless of registration order.

other.summary: Non-GET/HEAD requests now do filesystem lookups, so PermissionError gives 401 and a non-ENAMETOOLONG OSError gives 500 instead of the old unconditional 405
other.reason: get_response now calls _lookup_static_resource -> _lookup_path for non-GET methods. _lookup_path maps PermissionError to 401 and re-raises other OSErrors. The old code raised 405 before any lookup. This is reachable (unreadable files, symlink loops) but minor, and consistent with GET handling.
